nodes.name: Cobalt foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Cobalt foam (2 cm×1 cm×0.15 cm Tenerhui) was ultrasonicated with acetone, alcohol, 0.1 M HCl, and deionized water. It was then dried in an oven of 1 h at 60°C and directly employed as the electrodeposition substrate.

nodes.source_text: First, cobalt foam (2 cm×1 cm×0.15 cm Tenerhui) was ultrasonicated with acetone, alcohol, 0.1 M HCl, and deionized water. It was then dried in an oven of 1 h at 60°C...

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of cobalt hydroxide
nodes.procedure: 50 mL of cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (SigmaAldrich) solution (0.06 M) was chosen as electrolyte. Cobalt foam, platinum foil and Ag/AgCl were used as working, counter and reference electrodes for electrodeposition, respectively. The electrodeposition was utilized at -0.5 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode, RHE) with chronoamperometry for 30 min.

nodes.name: Co3O4/CC-h synthesis
nodes.procedure: To exclude the effect of cobalt foam substrate, carbon cloth (CC, Hesen) was chosen as substrate with the similar synthetic process of Co3O4/Co-h, and it was named Co3O4/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks assigned to spinel Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 43-1003) besides strong Co peaks for both Co₃O₄/Co-h and Co₃O₄/Co-l samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of Co₃O₄ were displayed in Fig. 1d. Except for strong diffraction peaks of Co, other smaller peaks of two samples could be assigned to spinel Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 43-1003).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XRD shows hydroxide to oxide transformation threshold at 150-200°C, with phase stability and crystallinity enhancement above 200°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the temperature increases to 400°C from room temperature, the threshold of hydroxides to oxides locates at 150∼200°C. Since 200°C, the phase doesn't change except for the enhancement of crystallinity...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals open-pore interlaced nanosheet structures for Co₃O₄/Co-h and Co₃O₄/Co-l; Co₃O₄/Co-h shows rougher nanosheets with ~20 nm nanoholes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images indicate both Co₃O₄/Co-h and Co₃O₄/Co-l display open-pore structures composed of interlaced nanosheets... compared with Co₃O₄/Co-l, the rough nanosheets of Co₃O₄/Co-h hold more ca. 20 nm nanoholes...

properties.description: High-magnification image showing fibrous or nanofiber morphology with dense, interwoven structure

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Co₃O₄/Co-h shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of ~0.24 nm and 0.29 nm assigned to (311) and (220) planes of Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image of Co₃O₄/Co-h displays distinct lattice fringe, and the interplanar spacing of ∼0.24 and 0.29 nm are assigned to the (311) and (220) planes of Co₃O₄, respectively.

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructure with yellow highlighted features

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED displays prominent diffraction rings corresponding to (440), (311), and (220) planes of Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) also displays prominent diffraction rings, corresponding to (440), (311), and (220) planes of Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms Co₃O₄/Co-h nanosheet thickness of about 6 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The AFM image (Fig. 2j) and height curve indicate that the Co₃O₄/Co-h nanosheet thickness is about 6 nm, validating the ultrathin and high anisotropic feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p peaks at ~780/795 eV (Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2), with 779.6/794.7 eV (Co³⁺) and 781.0/796.1 eV (Co²⁺) for both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a displays the high-resolution Co 2p spectra for two catalysts, and two peaks at around 780 and 795 eV correspond to the Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2, respectively. Furthermore, those peaks at 779.6 and 794.7 eV can be indexed to Co³⁺ while peaks at 781.0 and 796.1 eV correspond to Co²⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS fitted to peaks at 532.4 eV (Hydroxyl-O), 531.1 eV (Defective-O), 530.0 eV (Lattice-O); Co₃O₄/Co-h has 3% higher oxygen vacancy content than Co₃O₄/Co-l.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for Co₃O₄ O1s fine spectra (Fig. 3b), they can be fitted into three peaks centered at around 532.4, 531.1, and 530.0 eV... the fitted results display that Co₃O₄/Co-h is 3% higher than Co₃O₄/Co-l, indicating the former owns higher oxygen vacancies content.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows sharp signals at g=2.004 confirming oxygen vacancies; Co₃O₄/Co-h has higher intensity than Co₃O₄/Co-l.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both two spectra display sharp signals at a g-value of 2.004, showing the formation of oxygen vacancy... Compared with Co₃O₄/Co-l, higher intensity of Co₃O₄/Co-h spectrum means higher content of oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function of 3.66 eV for Co₃O₄/CC-h (lower than 3.84 eV for Co₃O₄/CC-l), indicating higher electron transfer rate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the UPS fitted results (Fig. 3d), the surface work function value of Co₃O₄/CC-h is 3.66 eV which is lower than Co₃O₄/CC-l (3.84 eV) and this indicates the former one possesses higher electron transfer rate.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates gives Cdl of 3.19 mF cm⁻² for Co₃O₄/Co-h (higher than 1.70 mF cm⁻² for Co₃O₄/Co-l), indicating more redox sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the fixed Cdl results (Fig.S7c), Co₃O₄/Co-h (3.19 mF cm⁻²) has a higher Cdl than that of Co₃O₄/Co-l (1.70 mF cm⁻²), demonstrating the former owns more redox sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smaller internal and charge transfer resistance for Co₃O₄/Co-h than Co₃O₄/Co-l.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, based on EIS results in Fig. 4g, both internal and charge transfer resistance of Co₃O₄/Co-h are smaller than Co₃O₄/Co-l, indicating Co₃O₄/Co-h owns a quicker electron transfer capability...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FTIR at -0.6 V shows bands at 1203 cm⁻¹ (NH₂OH), 1358 cm⁻¹ (NO⁻), negative band at 1370 cm⁻¹ (nitrate consumption), 1540 cm⁻¹ (NH₂ bending), 1694 cm⁻¹ (NH₄⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 6a shows the in situ FTIR spectra at the first 5 min (under the potential of -0.6 V vs RHE)... The band at around 1203 cm⁻¹ can assign to NH₂OH, and the band at ∼1358 cm⁻¹ corresponds to matrix NO⁻ formation; on the other hand, the wide negative band at 1370 cm⁻¹ matches well with the feature of nitrate consumption.
